To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the duration of mH and the duration of pHL are important factors in the development of auditory performance with CI, and that bilateral HAs can slow the central reorganization process.

(a) the performance of postlinguistically-deaf adults with a CI depends on the duration of m- and pHL, and on the brand of device; and (b) the use of bilateral HIs slows down central reorganization, and therefore, preserves the performance of post-linguistically deaf patients.

the performance of a postlingually deafened patient with a CI can be predicted by the following factors: 1) the pure tone average of the better ear before implantation, 2) the duration of mH, 3) the duration of pHL, 4) the use of HAs, 5) the brand of device and 6) the percentage of electrodes activated.

the duration of pHL, the duration of CI use and the brand of the CI are the main factors that affect CI performance.

a CI user is not only influenced by the duration of pHL, the age at implantation and the duration of CI experience but also by the duration of m HL, the use of HAs during the period of deafness, the brand of implant, and the percentage of electrodes activated.

The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance with a CI can be predicted from the preoperative factors.
the performance of postlinguistically-deaf patients with CI is a function of several factors that should all be taken into account in the design of future studies.
